messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish a complete, playable “Car For Sale Simulator” game, continuing from the interrupted build.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail matters.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained browser game using vanilla JavaScript, Three.js, HTML, and CSS.
- Game concept is a dealership simulator with driving, car inspection, negotiation, repairs, sales, upgrades, and saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a polished game interface and responsive styles.
- Added a Three.js town scene, dealership, market landmark, cars, and driving vehicle.
- Implemented game state, market/garage/office panels, inspection and negotiation modals, buying, repair, paint, selling, lot expansion, new-day market refresh, and local saves.

### Active
- Finish the driving/update loop and connect player movement, camera, interaction prompts, and HUD to the 3D world.
- Test the game in-browser, fix issues, and capture/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` currently ends with placeholder functions `tick()` and movement/interaction handling is not implemented; `initGame()` calls `tick()`, so the game is incomplete until this is finished.

## Next Move
1. Implement `tick()` with keyboard/touch driving, vehicle/camera updates, world clock, minimap/speed HUD, and market/dealership proximity prompts.
2. Implement `interact()` and make in-world interaction open the appropriate market, garage, or office panels.
3. Check for runtime errors and confirm complete play loop in a browser; save and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results for the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and page entry point.
- `style.css`: Game visuals, HUD, panels, and responsive layout.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js world and simulator logic; contains unfinished loop.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Bundled Three.js module.

## Objective
- Finish the existing “Car For Sale Simulator” as a complete, playable browser game.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG screenshot (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest; use a full-size PNG only if fine detail matters.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained game built with vanilla JavaScript, Three.js, HTML, and CSS.
- Game concept: dealership simulator with driving, car inspection, negotiation, repairs, sales, upgrades, and saved progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game interface in `index.html` and `style.css`, including HUD, navigation, panels, modals, mobile driving controls, and start screen.
- Added Three.js town-scene construction, dealership and market landmarks, cars, lighting, and camera setup in `src/main.js`.
- Implemented market/inventory data, save loading and saving, HUD updates, panels, inspection and negotiation flows, purchases, repairs, paint, sales, expansions, and daily market refresh.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` game loop, player driving, camera and HUD updates, proximity prompts, and interactions.
- Test the complete play loop in a browser, fix runtime issues, and capture/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- `src/main.js` currently ends after `sfxSuccess()`; `tick()` is still a placeholder, and `interact()` and remaining driving/update logic are not implemented. `initGame()` calls `tick()`, leaving the game incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Implement `tick()` with keyboard/touch driving, vehicle and camera updates, world clock, minimap/speed HUD, and market/dealership proximity prompts.
2. Implement `interact()` to open the appropriate market, garage, or office panels from the in-world prompts.
3. Run the game in a browser, fix runtime and play-loop issues, then capture and inspect the latest small JPEG.
4. Summarize assumptions and test results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and page entry point.
- `style.css`: Game visuals, HUD, panels, and responsive layout.
- `src/main.js`: Three.js world and simulator logic; driving loop and interaction handling remain unfinished.
- `vendor/three.module.js`: Bundled Three.js module.

- Changes are uncommitted.
